module purpose: neorv32_cache is a direct-mapped cache between a host request/response port pair (host_req_i, host_rsp_o) and a downstream bus port pair (bus_req_o, bus_rsp_i): a controller state machine sends accesses at or above UC_BEGIN, atomic and debug accesses straight to the bus, answers read hits from the neorv32_cache_memory sub-unit (valid bits, tags and data bytes), writes hits into the cache and through to the bus, downloads a missed block word by word from the bus, invalidates a block whose download reported an error, and clears all valid bits on a fence.

use-case flows.value: host access strobe or fence request, held pending while the controller is busy, that starts a lookup or a clear from S_IDLE
direct-access decision: accesses at or above UC_BEGIN, atomic or debug accesses sent to the bus and answered with the bus response
lookup and hit decision: valid bit and stored tag of the addressed block compared with the access tag
write: on a write hit the host byte enables and data are written into the cache word and the write is sent to the bus; a write miss is only sent to the bus

block download on a read miss: tag and index captured, each word requested from the bus at tag, index and offset and written into the cache, the block validated and tagged, the offset advanced until the last word
cached word returned to the host with an acknowledge on a read hit
download error: bus error responses accumulated during a download; the block invalidated and an acknowledge with error returned to the host
fence: all valid bits cleared and, when READ_ONLY = false, the fence forwarded to the bus
controller fields, valid bits and the read valid bit cleared while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Cache controller state -- which operation (idle, lookup, direct access, clear, download request, download response, download done) the controller is performing
conceptual assets.reasoning: `case ctrl.state is` (line 164) sequences every flow: the SELECTS records of ctrl.state (occurrence 4) choose bus_req_o.stb, cache_o.cmd_clr, cache_o.cmd_new, cache_o.cmd_inv, cache_o.we, host_rsp_o.ack and ctrl_nxt.state, among others. It is self-updating: `ctrl_nxt.state <= ctrl.state;` (line 136, CARRIES at occurrence 3) holds it, the arms at lines 169, 175, 188, 192, 196, 200, 203, 211, 221, 231, 246, 248, 258, 260 and 265 move it, `ctrl <= ctrl_nxt;` (line 126) registers it on rising_edge(clk_i) (line 125), and `ctrl.state <= S_IDLE;` (line 117) resets it. Integrity: each flow depends on the implemented transitions; for example the download sequence ends in the error check of line 254 before any host acknowledge (line 256) or re-lookup (line 260). A wrong state would acknowledge a host access without a lookup (lines 191, 256) or write the cache outside a download (line 237). Availability is also established under the implemented conditions: unknown states return to S_IDLE (line 265), while S_DIRECT_RSP and S_DOWNLOAD_RSP advance only on bus_rsp_i.ack (lines 210, 243). The map records CLOCKED_BY clk_i only on the whole record ctrl (occurrence 10, line 126; MAP CHECK lists it as receiving without driving), so ctrl.state is cited at occurrence 2, its reset arm inside the clocked process (line 117), with edge null. ctrl_nxt.state is the next-state computation whose result is stored in ctrl.state, so it is not an additional reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Block download address -- tag, index and word offset of the missed block being downloaded
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_LOOKUP the controller captures `ctrl_nxt.tag <= host_req_i.addr(31 downto 32-tag_size_c);` and the index (lines 180-181) and zeroes the offset (line 182). conceptual assets.reasoning: `valid_mem <= (others => '0');` on reset (line 377) and on clr_i (line 381), `valid_mem(to_integer(unsigned(acc_idx))) <= '0';` on inv_i (line 383) and the same assignment of '1' on new_i (line 385) define which blocks hold a completed download. `valid_mem_rd <= valid_mem(to_integer(unsigned(acc_idx)));` (line 387) reads the addressed bit, which gates the hit (line 405, GATES hit_o). The update commands clr_i, inv_i and new_i are reported with the allocation and invalidation concept; acc_idx is a slice of addr_i that indexes the array.

conceptual assets.concept: Block allocation and invalidation commands -- the controller's decisions to clear all blocks on a fence, validate and tag the block being downloaded, or invalidate it after a download error
conceptual assets.reasoning: neorv32_cache computes three commands, '0' by default (lines 146-148): `cache_o.cmd_clr <= '1';` in S_CLEAR (line 219), `cache_o.cmd_new <= '1';` in S_DOWNLOAD_REQ (line 226), and `cache_o.cmd_inv <= '1';` in S_DOWNLOAD_DONE when `ctrl.buf_err = '1'` (lines 254-255). They are delivered to clr_i, inv_i and new_i (lines 283-285). neorv32_cache_memory reads them to clear all valid bits (line 381), invalidate the addressed block (line 383), or validate it (line 385) and store its tag (lines 397-398), with clear taking priority over invalidate and invalidate over validate. Integrity: the valid and tag updates must follow exactly these decisions. A missing invalidate leaves an erroneous block valid, a spurious validate makes a block hit before its download, and a missing clear leaves blocks valid after a fence. Each cache_o field is computed here from a decision (SELECTED_BY ctrl.state, or GATED_BY ctrl.buf_err at occurrence 3), so the sub-unit wiring exception holds, and each computes its command. clr_i, inv_i and new_i set the commands in neorv32_cache_memory (GATES valid_mem, occurrence 2; new_i also GATES tag_mem at occurrence 3, line 397).

conceptual assets.concept: Cache hit decision -- whether the addressed block is valid and its stored tag equals the access tag
conceptual assets.reasoning: `hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0';` (line 405) computes the hit in neorv32_cache_memory, and hit_o drives cache_i.sta_hit (line 286). neorv32_cache tests it at `elsif (cache_i.sta_hit = '1') then` (line 189): on a hit a read is acknowledged from cached data (line 191) and a write updates the cache (line 194); on a miss a read starts a download (line 200). conceptual assets.concept: Cached data -- the bytes of each downloaded or written cache block, returned to the host on a read hit

conceptual assets.concept: Cache write enable -- which bytes of the addressed cache word are overwritten
conceptual assets.reasoning: `cache_o.we <= (others => '0');` by default (line 150), `cache_o.we <= host_req_i.ben;` on a write hit that is not a direct access (lines 186, 189-194), and `cache_o.we <= (others => '1');` while a downloaded word is stored (line 237).
